headline: Full-time work stands at 57.9 %, well under both benchmarks, but the overall picture is incomplete.
how_to_read: Flows run from all respondents (left) to employed or not employed (middle) and then to detailed situation (right); width is the share of respondents. Both branch totals are hidden, so branches appear as lower bounds (≥) and a hatched "Hidden" flow leaves "Respondents" directly.
key_findings: Full-time work accounts for 57.9 % of respondents.
Other employment, students, retirees and other situations are absent; part-time, self-employed and seeking work are hidden (fewer than 3 people).
benchmark: Full-time work is 16.7 pp below Asia (74.6 %) and 17.0 pp below all schools (74.9 %). Whether total employment also lags cannot be judged while the totals are hidden.
caveats: With n = 19, each person moves the percentages by several points, so the full-time gap should be read cautiously.
